featured_reviews.name: Farheen Darwesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I've been passing by the restaurant on the regular and always wanted to try it out. Honestly, I don't know why we didn't come here before. And now that we have, it's hand's down my favourite Sea food restaurant, in this part of town.

I really liked the whole vibe of the place, especially the hand painted murals on the 1st floor seating area. Comfortable seating, spacious yet cosy.

Their speciality being Mangalorean cuisine, we obviously had to try the staples! So we started with their superb Prawns Rava fry, coated and shallow fried in the most crunchy rava coating, is a must have. It was so good we ordered 3 plates! Same goes for their Prawns Koliwada fry, with delicious crispy bits of curry patta, adding an amazing punch of flavour! Both these come highly recommended by everyone.

You also must try their 'Sukkha Masala' - with any seafood of your choice. We went for their Teesria or clams. The masala has a heavy dose of fresh grated coconut, spices and well balanced flavors.

For the mains, Please do not leave without trying their Ghee Roast. It's the best I've had in Bombay. Right up there with the famous one from Nagarjuna, Bangalore.  Perfect roast masala with liberal amount of cashews in it. Best eaten with Neer Dosas. I just wish their quantity was a little more. It's just enough for one good eater.

The Prawn Gassi with Kori Roti is another Mangalorean speciality you cannot miss! Their Fish thalis are also very good and reasonable too.

The verdict: Superb food and good service are a delightful combination!

UPDATE: Visited the last two times and I'm sad to say that they lost the title for the best ghee roast. Since the chef changed, the dish is very mediocre, with maybe two-three bits  of cashews in it. :( Taste is not right too

featured_reviews.name: Reflections Photography Co.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Powai Lake, an artificial reservoir situated in the northern suburb of Powai, Mumbai, Maharashtra, stands as a significant urban waterbody amid the city’s bustling landscape. Constructed in 1891 by the British colonial administration, the lake was created by damming a tributary of the Mithi River between two hillocks to augment the drinking water supply for Bombay (now Mumbai). At the time of its inception, it spanned approximately 2.1 square kilometers (520 acres) with depths ranging from 3 meters at the periphery to 12 meters at its deepest point, and a catchment area of about 6.61 square kilometers.
Historically, Powai Lake served as a vital supplementary source of potable water and supported recreational activities such as angling and boating. Surrounded by lush greenery, the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay), and upscale developments like Hiranandani Gardens, it offers scenic views and a serene escape from urban chaos. The lake once harbored rich biodiversity, including diverse freshwater fish species, migratory and resident birds, marsh crocodiles, and native flora such as balsam bushes and aquatic plants.
Over time, rapid urbanization, untreated sewage inflow, garbage dumping, and invasive species like water hyacinth have led to eutrophication and degradation, rendering the water unfit for drinking. It is now primarily used for non-potable purposes, including gardening, industrial supply, and fishing. Ongoing revival efforts by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), environmental organizations, and community initiatives focus on desilting, weed removal, sewage diversion, and the establishment of treatment plants to restore its ecological health and recreational value. Despite challenges, Powai Lake remains a cherished natural asset, symbolizing the balance between urban development and environmental conservation in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: MR. SONU KUMAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
Powai Lake, located in the suburbs of Mumbai, is a scenic man-made lake that offers a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of city life. Constructed in 1891, this lake was originally intended to supply drinking water to the city, though it now serves primarily as a picturesque spot for recreation and relaxation.
The lake is surrounded by lush greenery, making it a popular destination for nature lovers, joggers, and families. The well-maintained promenade along the lake is perfect for a leisurely stroll, especially in the early mornings or evenings when the weather is pleasant. The view of the sunset over the water, with the backdrop of Mumbai's high-rises, is truly breathtaking.
Powai Lake is home to various species of birds and fish, making it a great spot for birdwatching. You can often see egrets, herons, and kingfishers in the area. The lake is also known for its population of crocodiles, though sightings are rare and safe distances are maintained.
In recent years, the area around the lake has seen significant development, with upscale residential complexes, cafes, and the prestigious IIT Bombay located nearby. Despite this, Powai Lake still retains its natural charm.
However, the lake has faced challenges related to pollution and encroachment over the years. Efforts have been made to clean and preserve the water, but there is still room for improvement in maintaining its ecological balance.
Overall, Powai Lake offers a tranquil retreat amidst the city's urban chaos. Whether you’re looking to unwind, enjoy nature, or simply take in the views, it's a must-visit spot for anyone in Mumbai.

Powai Garden is a refreshing green escape tucked away in one of Mumbai’s busiest and most upscale suburbs. Located close to Powai Lake, this garden offers a much-needed break from traffic, noise, and concrete, making it a favorite spot for locals of all age groups.

The garden is well-maintained, clean, and thoughtfully laid out, with lush lawns, shaded walking paths, and plenty of seating areas. Tall trees and greenery create a calm, soothing atmosphere, especially during early mornings and evenings. It’s an ideal place for morning walks, jogging, yoga, or light exercise, with many fitness enthusiasts regularly seen here.

For families, Powai Garden is a pleasant place to spend time together. Children can move around freely, and seniors often gather for relaxed walks or quiet conversations. The benches are strategically placed, allowing visitors to sit back and enjoy the fresh air or simply unwind after a long day.

One of the highlights of the garden is its peaceful vibe despite being in Powai, a highly developed and crowded area. The surroundings feel safe and community-oriented, and the overall environment encourages mindfulness and relaxation. Evening hours are particularly beautiful, with cooler breezes and a serene setting that contrasts sharply with the city’s fast pace.

While it’s not a large or touristy attraction, Powai Garden shines as a neighborhood green space that delivers exactly what it promises, calm, cleanliness, and comfort. With a little more lighting and minor upgrades, it could become even better, but as it stands, it already serves as a valuable oasis for residents.

featured_reviews.name: siddesh narvekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Powai Dam is a major reservoir located in Powai, a suburb in the northeastern part of Mumbai, India. It was built in 1891 by the British colonial government to supply drinking water to the city of Mumbai.

The dam is constructed across the Mithi River and covers an area of about 2.1 square kilometers. It has a height of approximately 26 meters and a length of 1,450 meters. The reservoir created by the dam has a capacity of 545 million gallons (2.48 million cubic meters) of water.

The Powai Dam is surrounded by lush greenery and provides a picturesque view. It serves as a popular recreational spot for locals and tourists, offering opportunities for boating and fishing activities. The dam also plays a crucial role in flood control, as it helps regulate the water flow during heavy rains.

Over the years, the Powai Dam has become an important landmark in Mumbai, attracting visitors with its serene atmosphere and scenic beauty. It is considered a significant source of water supply for the city and plays a vital role in meeting the water demands of its residents.

featured_reviews.review_text: Yes this hotel is famous for Non veg food but if you are vegitarian planning to visit this hotel with your Non vegitarian friends then please don't even think of going here. First up of all they have nothing to offer for veg people. They dont even allow veg people to eat tiffin if you are carrying one. I visited this place with my officer friends out of which only i was vegitarian but i was carrying my tiffin but rude and arrogant staff didn't allow me to eat my vegitarian tiffin. All they had for veg people is poor quality veg thali. Plus the place is congested with no AC which make your dining experience very bad.

featured_reviews.name: Syamchand Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love seafood, this is the place to be! It is a casual, no-frills restaurant specializing in Konkan seafood cuisine.

​We visited for lunch around noon and were able to place our order without any wait. However, by 12:30 PM, the restaurant was almost full, so plan your visit early to avoid a queue.
​We ordered several Thalis: Prawns Masala, Prawns Curry, and Surmai Curry, along with a plate of Surmai Fry. The Prawns Masala was awesome, and the other thalis were good too. The Surmai Fry came with two good-sized pieces and was amazing. 😍

​The outdoor seating area needs a bit of maintenance, but otherwise, it was a great dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Rebecca Lobo
featured_reviews.review_text: This place was once very popular and even frequented by Bollywood celebrities, but over the years the food quality and taste have declined. It’s definitely no longer worth the hype.

featured_reviews.name: Ravi kumar
featured_reviews.review_text: Great spicy food here. One of the risky items in non veg restaurants,  is getting fish food. We ordered pomfret fish fry meals. The fish was really fresh. So much that we ordered more of those items. Chapati with mutton sukka was awesome as well.  Great and must place for non veg food lovers. Closest cuisine is Chettinad cuisine, so south Indians will feel at ease and appreciate the food even more.

featured_reviews.name: ranjeet mahtani
featured_reviews.review_text:
The green curry thali. A more expensive variant is with a fried fish and some other accroutements.
The fried bombil - good quality, great portions and tasty.

featured_reviews.name: Aaditya Vyas
featured_reviews.review_text: Decent place for a quick bite, not worth going out of your way for. Fish was overcooked and tough, definitely not fresh. Had the bombil fry, prawns fry, bangda and rawas curries. Overall lacked flavour- even the solkadi was very diluted and bland.

featured_reviews.name: Anwitech Solutions
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good resturant... Typical konkani food ... Car parking is a big issue ... You need to resolve it your self

featured_reviews.name: Aakash Maji
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a very long time, I wasn’t filled with such a subtle and home-blend restaurant. Calling it a restaurant might be over exaggerating because this place is run by a family and the authentic Goan food that they serve just makes you feel at home. This charming place is nestled right beside the highway, amidst a small colony of homes. It’s seamlessly blended in, creating an atmosphere that feels more like a family’s home than a resting place.
We have got the Surmai Fish Curry Thali and the classic Chicken Masala Thali. Both were just amazing and homely to taste.

Their staffs are very friendly and sweet enough that you feel like home.

While the quantity of food didn’t quite match the pricing, the quality was great.

This is very good place to recommend for a family lunch/dinner. I am sure you won’t be disappointed with it. Enjoy.

featured_reviews.name: Nishad lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very limited seating hence waiting time could be more. Service was good.
Food was very good and fresh. Bombil were delicious. Surmai thali, tandoor surmai thali was delicious. Prawns Koliwada was very good too. Chicken thali was delicious. Overall a great experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sanjana Bag
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bombil fry was crispy and delicious, with three pieces served—quite satisfying. The Prawns Koliwada arrived hot and tasted really good. The Surmai tawa fry was just okay, nothing exceptional but decent.
The highlight was the Prawns Masala Thali. It is very cost-friendly and offers great value for money. The thali includes a good variety of items such as rice, three breads of your choice, prawns curry, papad, sukha machi, thecha, and sol kadi.

featured_reviews.name: Chanchal Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the Mutton Thali, Chicken Malai Kebab, and Bombil Fish Fry—all absolutely worth it. Had to wait around 10 minutes, but the wait was totally justified. Service was quick, food came hot, and the seating is comfortable. Really liked how well they’ve managed the seating arrangement. Overall, a satisfying experience.

featured_reviews.name: Suvas Wagh
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a great place to have sea food in Mumbai. They have Multiple outlets in Mumbai. I visited this place with friends. Tried Surmai fry, Pomfret thali, Prawns thali, Prawns kolowada, Chicken lollipop and Chicken thali. We loved the food! All the fish served was very fresh and perfectly fried with amazing taste. Even the chicken tasted great. Also the quantity of food is good compared to cost, it can be improved. Service is also good. Might face waiting time of upto 15-20 mins on weekends.

But recommend to try their sea food.

featured_reviews.name: Masban Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the best places for seafood lover’s especially the thali. My family and I have been her a number of time and this place doesn’t disappoint. Our favourites are the Surmai thali, shimpy thali, pomfret thali bombil thali and prawns thali. The portions size are decent and reasonably priced. You have options of bhakri, neer dosa or chapatis with the thali. We try and visit here at least once a month.

featured_reviews.name: Dipesh Malvade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Jaihind Lunch Home, Bandra today and it turned out to be a super satisfying food experience! 🤩🍽️✨
The restaurant gives a classic Mumbai dining vibe with a lively and welcoming atmosphere 🏙️🎶. Even though the place was quite busy, the service was quick, smooth and well managed 👏⚡
⭐ What I Ordered:
🍗 Chicken Lapeta Kebab – ₹390
Absolutely delicious! Perfectly grilled, juicy, smoky and nicely spicy 🌶️🔥. Every bite was full of flavour and cooked to perfection 🤤👌 Definitely a must-try if you love spicy starters!
🥘 Sukha Chicken Thali – ₹430
Authentic coastal style dish with rich and balanced flavours 🌴🍗. It felt like proper home-style Maharashtrian food 🏡❤️. Very filling, satisfying and full paisa vasool meal 😋
🥞 Neer Dosa (3 pcs) – ₹90
Soft, light, smooth and paired perfectly with the main dish 🧈🥥. Simple but very tasty and fresh ✨
🥥 Solkadhi – ₹90
Super refreshing, cool and perfectly balanced the spice level 🧊🥤🌸 Loved the taste and freshness!
💧 Mineral Water – ₹35
💰 Total Bill – ₹1087 💳🧾
Overall, the food quality, taste, portion size and service were really impressive ⭐👏. The place is perfect for family dining 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, friends outing 👫 and casual food plans 🍛🍹
If you are in Bandra and love authentic Maharashtrian & coastal food, you definitely need to visit 😉📍🍴

featured_reviews.name: vicky s
featured_reviews.review_text: I took surmai tawa thali. The surmai was fresh. The fish curry was yummy. Bhakri could have been better. Surmai, curry and rice together tasted heavenly. Must visit for fish lovers in BKC.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.
